clue.text: Cryptic Elgar, 1A "Eating out tagine here?"

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscure and puzzling, so the letters that follow are scrambled out of their plain order

parts.note: the composer's name taken as written
the digit one looks like the letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about Elgar, as if he wondered where to go for a North African dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: '1A' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is simply the letters I and A joining Elgar in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagine is the slow-cooked stew of North Africa, so a country of the Maghreb is a likely place to dine on it.

clue.text: Notorious Biblical king to upset American historian

parts.note: Herod ordered the Massacre of the Innocents in the Gospels

indicators.note: to upset something is to tip it over, so in a down clue the word is turned the other way up

parts.note: taken as written before turning
standard abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A wicked king of the Bible sets out to annoy a scholar from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American historian' reads as one person, but American only supplies two letters and 'historian' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Herodotus was the Greek writer often called the father of history, so he is a celebrated example of a historian.

clue.text: Fearsome warrior finishes off Attic lad

indicators.note: to finish off here means to take away the final letter of each following word

parts.note: Attic loses its last letter
lad loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A terrifying fighter kills off a young man from ancient Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishes off' looks like a violent verb in the story, but it instructs you to trim the tail from each of the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila was the fifth-century leader of the Huns, remembered as one of history's most feared conquerors.

clue.text: Piercing stomach is mostly a show of virility

indicators.note: a piercing runs through the flesh, so the answer passes straight through the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word, the whole middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A navel piercing worn mainly as a display of masculine toughness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piercing' sounds like the body jewellery, but it signals letters threaded through 'stomach is mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is exaggerated, swaggering masculinity, a display of manly strength and aggression.

clue.text: My daughter's in on arranging a special time for mum

indicators.note: arranging means putting things into a new order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: all fifteen letters used, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A parent notes that their daughter is involved in planning a treat for her mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of the first four words is used; the surface even describes what a daughter would do on the day itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Mothering Sunday is the British name for Mother's Day, falling in Lent, when mothers are honoured with gifts and cards.

clue.text: Musical group that contains 32 men?

parts.note: Chess is a 1980s stage musical by the ABBA songwriters with Tim Rice
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: A question about a band or choir with thirty-two male members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical group' reads as a band, but it splits into a show title and a word for a collection. Chess pieces are traditionally called men, sixteen per side.
explanation.definitionFit: A full board game kit holds sixteen pieces per player, and those pieces are conventionally known as men.

clue.text: This compiler would put on Isle of Man dialect

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: I would, shortened to I'd
standard abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: The setter claims they would adopt a Manx way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'this compiler' means the setter, so it gives I, here as I'd. The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom can mean the particular form of language used by a people or region, which is what a dialect is.

clue.text: Produced content of viral Portuguese product

parts.note: past tense of make, meaning produced

indicators.note: the content of a thing is what lies inside it, so the outer letters are thrown away

parts.note: the inner letters without the first and last

explanation.surface: Someone created online material that went viral, about some Portuguese goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' and 'viral' suggest internet posts, but 'content of' just keeps the inside of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine made on the Portuguese island of the same name, a classic export of that country.

clue.text: Person engaging lawyer Neil is back in court

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court

indicators.note: going back means running in the opposite direction, so the name is read from right to left

parts.note: the name taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: Someone hiring a solicitor named Neil finds himself in court again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lawyer Neil' reads as one person, but the lawyer belongs to the definition and Neil is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is the customer of a professional, such as the person who retains a solicitor or barrister.

clue.text: Classic 1963 film flyers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Alfred Hitchcock's horror film about attacking gulls and crows
second meaning: feathered creatures that fly, with the article

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one film about aviators, but the year and 'classic' make one meaning and 'flyers' stands alone as the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's 1963 thriller bears this title, and winged animals in general are the creatures that take to the air.

clue.text: Tear down his model furiously

indicators.note: acting furiously means violently and wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: all eight letters used

explanation.surface: In a rage, someone smashes up the model another person built.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface already describes destruction, so the definition and the anagram signal tell the same story.
explanation.definitionFit: To demolish a building is to knock it to the ground, which is exactly what tearing a structure down means.

clue.text: Top meeting involving key players

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the highest point of a mountain
second meaning: a conference between heads of government

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top meeting' reads as one high-level gathering, but 'Top' is a separate meaning on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the peak of a hill and a conference of world leaders, the most senior figures in politics.

clue.text: Relic from bygone age Rodin's sculpted, lined with gold

indicators.note: something lined with a material has it inside, so one piece sits within the other
sculpted means shaped and remodelled, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: the sculptor's name with its possessive s, ignoring the apostrophe
Au is the chemical symbol for gold, from Latin aurum

explanation.surface: An ancient artefact that Rodin carved and gilded on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodin was a sculptor, so 'sculpted' fits the surface perfectly while really telling you to rearrange his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally an extinct reptile from prehistoric times, and figuratively a person or thing that is hopelessly out of date.

clue.text: Maybe 99 or 100 brought in, that is best

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so it goes within the other letters

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: A scoring report: ninety-nine or a century made, which is the best result.
explanation.walkthrough: '99 or 100' looks like a cricket score, but 99 belongs to the definition and 100 is a Roman numeral. A 99 is a British soft-serve cone with a chocolate flake pushed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A 99 is one kind of soft whipped frozen dessert in a cone, so 'maybe' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Might Rod come up with this ginger, ridiculous hairstyle?

definitions.text: Might Rod come up with this

parts.note: ginger hair is red hair
a mullet is the short-at-the-front, long-at-the-back cut much mocked since the 1980s

explanation.surface: A question whether someone called Rod might invent a silly ginger haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like a man's name, perhaps Rod Stewart with his famous spiky hair, but it is a fishing rod hauling up a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Red mullet is a prized sea fish, so it is something an angler's rod might bring up out of the water.

clue.text: Noble Conservative featured in Ustinov broadcast

indicators.note: to be featured in something is to appear within it, so one letter goes inside
broadcast once meant scattering seed widely, so the letters are strewn about

parts.note: the actor's surname taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: An aristocratic Tory appears in a programme with Peter Ustinov on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits Ustinov the actor and raconteur, but it shuffles his name around the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a British peer ranking below an earl and above a baron, so he is a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Pan cooks white fish after downing fine German wine

indicators.note: downing something means knocking it out, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: cooking in a pan is frying
F is the pencil grading abbreviation for fine
ling is a long white-fleshed sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A chef fries some fish after knocking back a glass of good German white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downing' looks like drinking, which suits a wine clue, but it removes the F from the cooking word.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape variety and the wine made from it, famously grown along the Rhine and Mosel.

clue.text: One from Lisbon turned up on board debonair e-bike

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means flipped so it reads from bottom to top
passengers on board are inside the vessel, so the letters sit within the words

parts.note: the letters running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A man from Lisbon arrives riding a stylish electric bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as arrived, but in a down clue it means the hidden letters run upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is in Portugal, which shares the Iberian peninsula with Spain, so a Lisbon native is an Iberian.

clue.text: One born in the Fifties eating large white loaf

indicators.note: something eating another thing has it inside, so one letter goes within

parts.note: a baby boomer was born in the post-war population surge
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A middle-aged person tucking into a big slice of white bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large white loaf' reads as one item, but 'large' belongs to the wordplay and only 'white loaf' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a British crusty bread with diagonal slashes across its rounded top, usually made with white flour.

clue.text: One way to make egg: beat it regularly Bill before beginning to eat

parts.note: scram is slang for go away, as is beat it

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first and third letters of the name

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cookery tip: whisk the eggs regularly, Bill, before you sit down to your meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat it' looks like whisking the egg, but it is slang for clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble eggs is to stir them while cooking, one of the standard ways of preparing them alongside frying and poaching.

clue.text: Russian emperor takes exercise after throwing up meal

indicators.note: thrown up in a down clue means sent upwards, so the letters read bottom to top
to take something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: the tsar was the ruler of imperial Russia
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: A tsar goes for a workout after vomiting up his dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing up' sounds like being sick, but in a down clue it lifts the whole assembly upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Repast is a formal or old-fashioned word for a meal, the food eaten at one sitting.

clue.text: Putrefying triceps wound after dislocating radius

indicators.note: wound as the past of wind means twisted round, so the letters are turned about
dislocating means putting out of place, so a letter is knocked out

parts.note: the arm muscle taken as written
r is the standard symbol for radius

explanation.surface: An injury to the arm muscle festers after a bone is put out of joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' and 'radius' look like anatomy: a cut and a forearm bone. Read 'wound' as twisted, and radius as its symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Septic describes tissue infected with bacteria and decaying, which is what putrefying means.

clue.text: Sample refinement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to try a little of food or drink
second meaning: discernment and good judgement in aesthetic matters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sample refinement' reads as testing some polish; the two words are separate meanings, one a verb and one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means trying a morsel with the tongue and also cultured discernment, as in a person of good taste.

clue.text: Noel, ordinary dad, knight, retired general

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the name taken as written
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
pa is an informal word for father
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A roll call: Noel, an ordinary father, a knight and a retired army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired general' reads as an old soldier, but 'retired' turns the whole string back and 'general' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the French military commander who became emperor, among history's most famous generals.

clue.text: Popular recording group The Killers

parts.note: a hit is a successful record
a squad is a group or team

explanation.surface: The Killers, the American rock band, described as a chart-topping act.
explanation.walkthrough: The Killers is the name of a real rock band, which suits the music surface, but read literally it means a gang of murderers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit squad is a team of assassins sent to murder someone, so its members are literally killers.

clue.text: Sharp stick Kelvin poked into drain

indicators.note: something poked into another thing ends up inside it

parts.note: a sewer is a drain for waste water
K is the symbol for the kelvin unit of temperature

explanation.surface: Someone named Kelvin jabs a pointed stick down a drain to clear it.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelvin looks like a person's name, but it is the SI unit of temperature, giving its symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a pointed rod of metal or wood used to hold pieces of food together while cooking.

clue.text: Advances, trying to hold line

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the answer sits within the clue's own words

parts.note: the letters running from inside the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Progress is being made, with effort, to keep someone on the phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advances' looks like the definition, but it is only the container; 'line' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A line can mean a family's descent through generations, such as a royal line, which is one's lineage or forebears.
